chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Muhraz al-Kha'thami, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a girl from whom a man derives pleasure (temporary marriage), he said: Yes, unless she is a young girl who is deceived (due to immaturity). I said: May God perfect you, what is the limit at which, when she reaches it, she is not considered deceived? He said: A daughter of ten years. And among the reasons is that the report may have been issued in the manner of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah).
ai.seo_question: What is the age of maturity for temporary marriage in Shia fiqh according to the hadith of Muhammad ibn Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* establishes the age of maturity for temporary marriage (mut'ah) as ten years, defining the threshold where a girl is no longer considered 'deceived' (tukhdah) due to immaturity. The narrator notes that this ruling may be based on *taqiyyah* (precautionary dissimulation), reflecting the scholarly debate on whether this age is a definitive legal limit or a cautious estimate. This narration is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the eligibility of young girls for mut'ah contracts.
